response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.dealedge AS side, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS n FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.dealedge), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM c) SELECT SUM(c.n) AS total_count, AVG(c.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.n > a.avg_n

assumptions.assumption: Orders with a NULL dealedge form their own group (a NULL side) and are included in the per-side counts and the average across sides, since GROUP BY keeps NULL as a group. If no orders have a NULL side this has no effect.
Distinct orders are identified by orders.recordvault, which is the unique order reference. The average is taken over the sides that have at least one matched order.
If no side is above the average (all counts equal), the query returns one row with NULL values.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude orders with a NULL side from the grouping, so only real sides (Buy, Sell) are counted and averaged.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.dealedge AS side, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS n FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault WHERE o.dealedge IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.dealedge), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg_n FROM c) SELECT SUM(c.n) AS total_count, AVG(c.n - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.n > a.avg_n
